blocks.text: Event Overview

Vendor Selections
Venue: The Meridian Conference Center — $18,400 (room rental + AV package)
Catering: Harvest Table Catering — $9,775 (breakfast, lunch, afternoon break; $115/head)
AV/Production: ClearSignal AV — $4,200 (full-day tech support, livestream to 2 overflow rooms)
Floral/Décor: Bloom & Branch Studio — $1,850 (dinner reception centerpieces, lobby arrangements)
Photography: Lena Park Photography — $2,100 (half-day, keynote + group shots)
Budget Actuals
Total spend: $38,620. Original budget: $40,000. Came in $1,380 under budget. Rachel's planning fee: $4,500 (flat rate, corporate tier).
Post-Event Notes

Client satisfaction: 4.6/5. AV and catering received top marks. Floral vendor (Bloom & Branch) did not match agreed arrangement style for dinner reception — client flagged this. Registration area felt cramped for 85 pax; recommend requesting the pre-function foyer for 100+ headcount. Overall smooth execution. Client confirmed interest in rebooking for 2026.
Standing Client Preferences
Prefers full-day Friday or Saturday format to minimize weekday disruption
Requires dedicated quiet room for executive prep/green room
Dietary: 12 vegetarian, 3 vegan, 2 gluten-free — must be clearly labeled
Branded signage and printed programs required (client provides assets by T-3 weeks)
No hard alcohol at lunch; wine/beer acceptable at dinner reception only

title: Veridian Technologies — Client Profile

blocks.text: Client Background

Veridian Technologies is a mid-size B2B SaaS company (~320 employees) focused on HR and workforce management software. HQ in downtown Boston. Primary event contact is Marcus Chen, VP of People Operations — responsive, detail-oriented, approves budgets internally before sign-off from CFO.
Event History
2024: Q4 All-Hands (offsite, 60 pax) — The Langham Boston. Budget: $22,000. Smooth execution, first engagement.
2025: Annual Leadership Summit (85 pax) — The Meridian. Budget: $40,000 actual $38,620. Strong outcome, client re-engaged for 2026.
Decision-Making Notes

Marcus has budget authority up to ~$45K; anything above requires CFO sign-off (Priya Nair). Proposal must include itemized line-item breakdown — Marcus shares directly with finance. Turnaround from proposal to signed contract has been 10–14 days in prior engagements. Prefers PDF proposals with a one-page executive summary up front.
Communication Preferences

Email preferred for formal comms. Responsive within same business day. Occasional Zoom check-ins (30 min max). Does not use project management tools — all coordination via email and shared Google Drive folder.

title: Vendor Notes — Bloom & Branch Studio (Rate Conflict Log)

blocks.text: Rate Increase — Spring 2026
Sophie notified Rachel ~April 14 that wholesale costs (labor + imported stems) have risen significantly. New rate structure: +18% across all packages. Formal email received April 23.
Affected Weddings & Dollar Impact

1. Kowalski-Reyes (May 9): Contracted $3,500 → new rate ~$4,130. Delta: +$630.
2. Chen-Okafor (Jun 27): Contracted $3,800 → new rate ~$4,484. Delta: +$684.
3. Patel-Williams (Aug 23): Contracted $4,100 → new rate ~$4,838. Delta: +$738.
Commitment Audit
Client-side (Dana Kowalski): Verbal price-hold assurance given Feb 18 at contract signing. Supported by signed contract at $3,500 — written instrument. Stronger commitment.

Vendor-side (Sophie Marchetti): Verbal assurance ~Apr 19 phone call that Rachel would 'work with them' on new rates across all three weddings. No written record. Weaker commitment — relational, not contractual.
Resolution Options

Option A — Absorb delta from contingency (Kowalski-Reyes only): $630 delta fits within $800 contingency. Honors client price-hold. Renegotiate with Sophie for a Kowalski-Reyes carve-out at contracted rate; apply new rate only to Chen-Okafor and Patel-Williams where there is more lead time for client disclosure.

Option B — Disclose to Dana with options memo: Transparent disclosure of rate increase, offer three options (absorb, substitute florist, partial scope reduction). Preserves trust but risks client distress 2 weeks pre-event.
Option C — Source substitute florist: See Obsidian florist-alternatives note. Risky at 13 days out — availability and style match uncertain.
Recommended Path

Pursue Option A for Kowalski-Reyes: negotiate carve-out with Sophie, absorb $630 from contingency, do not disclose to Dana. For Chen-Okafor and Patel-Williams: proactive client disclosure with revised budget options — sufficient lead time exists. Do NOT repeat dual-assurance pattern.
